593:
It is the purpose of this article to protect the public health, safety, and general welfare of individuals and the community at large; to establish uniform regulations for the operation of mobile food service units, and to enhance street-level economic opportunities within the city.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
594:
This article shall apply to the operation of all mobile food service units within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
595:
The following words, terms and phrases as used in this article shall mean:
Base of operation means a food service establishment, or any other permitted location in which food, containers or supplies are kept, handled, prepared, packaged, stored, or placed in containers for subsequent transport, sale or service elsewhere.
Canteen truck means vehicles that operate to provide retail sales of fully cooked foods and nonalcoholic beverages.
Fixed food service establishment means a nonmobile public or private establishment which prepares and serves meals, lunches, short orders, sandwiches, frozen desserts, or other edible products directly to the consumer either for carryout or service within the establishment. The term includes restaurants, coffee shops, cafeterias, short-order cafes, luncheonettes, taverns, lunchrooms, places which retail sandwiches or salads, soda fountains, and similar facilities by whatever name called. This term shall not apply to establishments offering food service incidental to their operations.
Food truck encompasses all mobile food service units with the exception of pushcarts. Food trucks shall be no larger than 30 x eight feet.
Mobile food service unit means a trailer, pushcart, vehicle vendor or any other similar conveyance operating as an extension of and under the managerial authority of the permit holder of its permitted base of operation. The mobile food service unit and its permitted base of operation together make a mobile food service establishment.
Parking space means an unimpeded area having minimum dimensions of 18 feet in length and nine feet in width which is readily accessible at all times for the parking and removal of a motor vehicle without the necessity of moving another vehicle;
Pushcart means a human propelled, self-contained, enclosed food service cart that operates at pre-determined locations as approved by the health authority and the City of Douglas. Pushcarts shall be no larger than five x ten feet.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
597:
Review and consideration of an application shall be conducted in accordance with principles of due process. Applications may be denied where an applicant fails to demonstrate that he or she meets the conditions and requirements of this article, or where an applicant fails to comply with applicable local, state or federal law. Any false statements, material omissions or substantially misleading information provided in an application or furnished by an applicant in connection with an application constitute grounds for any one or combination of the following sanctions: denial; refusal to renew; revocation; suspension; and imposition of penalties.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
598:
(a) Food trucks—Mobile food service unit. The following operational requirements and conditions apply to food trucks and mobile food service units.
(1) Food trucks shall not conduct business within ten feet from the public right-of-way, with the exception of special events recognized by the City of Douglas for which the food truck has received pre-approval from the city manager.
(2) Food trucks shall not operate within a landscape buffer.
(3) Food trucks shall not operate within 20 feet of an intersection or cross walk.
(4) Food trucks shall not operate within ten feet of any driveway or other curb cut access, loading zone, bus stop, or within a fire lane.
(5) Food trucks shall not operate within 15 feet of a building entrance.
(6) Food trucks shall not operate in front of display window of a fixed location business.
(7) Food trucks shall not operate within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
(8) Food trucks shall not operate within ten feet of any parking space or access ramp designated for persons with disabilities
(9) Food trucks shall not operate on private property without the written consent of the property owner.
(10) Food truck and mobile food service units shall not operate within ten feet of any building, structure, vehicles and/or combustible materials.
(11) No operator or employee of a food truck may, at any time, utilize amplified sound devices.
(12) Food trucks shall comply with the city's grease interceptor standards, as set forth in the Code, rules and/or regulations, as amended. Refer chapter 38, division 5, fats, oil and grease for food service and processing establishments, sections 38-477 through 38-581.
(13) The Georgia Department of Public Health mobile food service unit permit, together with all applicable health certificates, including food inspection reports, pertaining to the unit, shall be firmly attached in a prominent location, which shall be plainly visible to the public at all times the food truck is conducting business.
(14) Food trucks may conduct business only within the zones designated for such activity set forth in the zoning section of the City Code, as amended.
(15) When conducting business, food trucks shall provide no less than nine feet of unobstructed horizontal pedestrian clearance on private property, as measured from the main service window.
(16) Food trucks may not be left unattended or otherwise stored on sites at which they offer the sale of food and beverage to the public unless allowed by the zoning ordinance. All mobile food service units must return to their base of operations when not in use.
(17) Food trucks shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal health and safety laws, regulations, and rules.
(18) Food trucks may place one temporary sandwich board for advertisement purposes no more than four feet from the main service window.
(19) Food trucks may not conduct business in a location that might block or impede either pedestrian or vehicular traffic.
(20) Food trucks may not conduct business with any person while such person is situated in a motor vehicle.
(21) Toilet facilities. Toilet facilities, including hand washing stations must be provided for employees and consumers. See Georgia Department of Public Health Rule 511-6-1-.06(2)(h). Toilet facilities may be no more than 200 feet away from the food truck and/or mobile food service unit. The hand washing station shall be no more than 25 feet away from the food truck and/or mobile food service unit.
(b) Push carts. The following operational requirements and conditions apply to push carts:
(1) No operator or employee of a push cart may, at any time, utilize amplified sound devices.
(2) The Georgia Department of Public Health mobile food service unit permit, together with all applicable health certificates, including food inspection reports, pertaining to the unit, shall be firmly attached in a prominent location, which shall be plainly visible to the public at all times the push cart is conducting business.
(3) Push carts may conduct business only within the zones designated for such activity set forth in the zoning section of the City Code.
(4) When conducting business, push carts shall provide no less than six feet of unobstructed horizontal pedestrian clearance on private property, as measured from the main service window or cart.
(5) Push carts shall comply with all applicable local, state and federal health and safety laws, regulations and rules.
(6) Push carts may not display signage not affixed to the cart itself.
(7) Push carts may not conduct business in a location that might block or impede either pedestrian or vehicular traffic.
(8) Push carts may not conduct business with any person while such person is situated in a motor vehicle.
(9) Push carts may not furnish temporary seating.
(10) Vendors operating from registered push carts are permitted to sell food only, except during approved special events. Push carts may operate in only approved areas of the city.
The community development director is authorized to determine the appropriate placement of push carts within the authorized and assigned areas and may require inappropriately placed push carts to be removed.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
599:
(a) Each mobile food service unit shall provide a suitably-sized receptacle for litter, which shall be located within ten feet of the service window of the unit. It shall be maintained and regularly emptied. All waste generated by the mobile food service unit's operation, including that associated with its customers and staff, must be disposed of at the base of operation.
(b) The area within which a mobile food service unit operates shall, at all times, be kept clean and free from litter, garbage, rubble and debris. For purposes of this section, a mobile food service unit shall be responsible for maintaining in a safe and hygienic manner, the premises on which it is situated.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
600:
To minimize the threat to public safety posed by fire, the following apply:
(a) Combustible gas detector. Prior to the operation of any combustible gas-fueled appliances, all visible connections shall be inspected by a licensed third-party for leakage utilizing a combustible gas detector. Detected leaks shall be repaired before any gas-fueled appliance is operated.
(b) Propane cylinders. Propane and natural gas tanks shall be shut off while the mobile food vehicle is in motion, unless the tank is equipped with an impact detection shut-off device approved by the U.S. DOT. Propane and natural gas tanks must always be shut off while the vehicle is unattended and/or in overnight storage. Mounted tanks must be secure (NFPA 58—5.2.4) and conform with NFPA standards relating to the safe mounting of tanks as described in NFPA 58—6.23.3.3. and be capable of withstanding impact requirements as required by the NFPA (NFPA 58—6.23.3.4.) Portable gas containers must be secured, at all times, to the mobile food service unit, push cart, in the upright position, to prevent the containers from tipping over.
(c) Portable fire extinguishers. All mobile food service units shall be equipped with a readily accessible multipurpose dry chemical portable fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of 2A 10BC. All mobile food service units utilizing fats or cooking oils, including those that produce grease, grease laden vapors or oily byproducts, shall, in addition to the ABC fire extinguisher, be equipped with a readily accessible Class K portable fire extinguisher. All required fire extinguishers shall be maintained in compliance with National Fire Protection Association 10, as amended.
(d) Operations prior to set up. Propane and natural gas tanks shall be shut off while the mobile food vehicle is in motion unless the tank is equipped with an impact detection shut-off device approved by the U.S. DOT. Mobile food service units are prohibited from igniting, starting or operating any cooking appliances requiring heat, electricity or combustible gases while traveling upon any street, road or highway. Food warming or hot-holding appliances are exempt from this requirement.
(e) Smoke-free air. Mobile food service units shall comply with the clean indoor air ordinance, as amended.
(f) Exhaust creating nuisance. Emission of exhaust gases or smoke shall not be handled in such a manner as to constitute a nuisance.
(g) An approved fire suppression system must be installed when an exhaust hood system is required.
(h) An exhaust hood system shall be installed above all commercial cooking appliances used for commercial purposes that produce grease vapors.
(i) Hood cleaning and maintenance. Mobile food service units shall be maintained and regularly cleaned to minimize the buildup of grease and other combustible residues. This includes all interior and exterior surfaces upon which grease can or may accumulate including, but not limited to, hold filter surfaces, plenums, ducts, exhaust fans, and exterior cowling.
(j) Fire suppression system inspections. All mobile food service unit fire suppression systems shall be inspected and maintained in accordance with the applicable provisions of the National Fire Protection Association. The system shall be tagged in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Georgia Safety Fire Commissioner.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
601:
The city manager may permit licensed mobile food service units to operate at special events pursuant to the City of Douglas's special events policy and procedures. The City of Douglas shall be listed as an additional insured certificate holder for any mobile food service unit operating on the public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)

(a) The city marshal shall maintain a record of all code violation charges, founded accusations and convictions concerning mobile food service units. When a mobile food service unit owner or operator accumulates three code violations for a particular mobile service unit within a period of 12 consecutive months, the city shall revoke the mobile food service unit's location approvals, permit or occupation tax certificate and reject all applications for mobile food service unit location approvals by the concerned owner(s) and operator(s) for a period of 12 consecutive months following the date of revocation.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accessory structure means a subordinate building or structure on the same lot, or part of the main building, occupied by or devoted to an accessory use.
Booth means a structure constructed for the purpose of displaying and selling merchandise.
Building means a structure having a roof, supported by columns or by walls and intended for the shelter, housing, or enclosure of any person, animal, or chattel.
Building inspector means the building inspector of the city or the building inspector's authorized representative.
Common area means any area or space designed for the joint use of tenants occupying flea markets.
Enclosed structure means a building enclosed on all sides with permanent walls and a permanent roof.
Enforcing agencies means Douglas Police Department, code enforcement division and/or community development director, the building inspector, and the Douglas Fire Department of the city; and the county health department; charged by law with the duty to enforce the provisions of this article.
Flea market stand means that part of an individual lot that has been reserved for the placement of flea market booths, appurtenant structures or additions.
Flea markets means an indoor or outdoor flea markets as defined herein.
Gross sales area means the sum of all areas of the flea market not devoted to parking, roadways, yard setback requirements, or open space. For the purpose of determining gross sales area, open space is defined as a continuous unit of land of at least one acre in area that is not used for any function of the flea market. Gross sales area includes all parts of all buildings in the flea market.
Market management means the person who owns, or has charge, care or control of the flea market.
Outdoor flea market means a principal commercial activity that occurs at a fixed location, where a proprietor, partnership, or corporation leases to vendors a booth or commercial stall from which the vendor markets his or her goods. Part or all of the flea market is conducted outside of an enclosed structure; sidewalk sales are not included under this definition. Each vending location shall have access via an internal walkway, courtyard, path, or common area.
Prepared food sales means the sale of any food item subjected to a special process or treatment (ex: heating, frying, mixing, slicing, etc.) before being sold to the consumer, and generally intended for consumption on the flea market premises.
Public street means a public way which affords principal means of access to abutting properties.
Retail food sales means the sale of nonprepared, fresh food items (i.e., produce, farm products, seafood, and meat) not generally intended for consumption on the flea market premises.
Right-of-way means an area, either public or private, over which the legal right of passage exists.
Service buildings means a structure housing sanitary, operational, office, recreational, maintenance and other facilities built to conform to required standards.
Structure includes "arranged," "designed," "constructed," "altered," "converted," "rented," "leased," or "intended to be used."
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023; Ord. No. 12232024, 12-23-2024)
610:
The City of Douglas Police Department, city marshal's office, Douglas Fire Department, building inspector, and code enforcement officers can make inspections as necessary to determine satisfactory compliance with this article as authorized by all city codes.

613:
Whenever the chief of police, city marshal, chief of fire department, or building inspector finds that an emergency exists which requires immediate action to protect the public health, including violations of any of the applicable rules and regulations of the county health department or the state department of public health, they may without notice or hearing issue an order reciting the existence of such an emergency, and requiring that such action be taken as he or she may deem necessary to meet the emergency, including the suspension of the occupational tax certificate, permits or licenses. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this article, such order shall be effective immediately. Any person to whom such an order is directed shall comply therewith immediately, but upon petition to the board of zoning appeals, such person shall be afforded a hearing as soon as possible.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
614:
Any person violating or neglecting or refusing to comply with any of the provisions of this article shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished according to the general penalties described in section 1-11. Each day that a violation is permitted to exist shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
617:
(a) Building permit. It shall be unlawful for any person to locate a flea market or to construct, alter or extend any flea market within the limits of the city unless such person holds a valid building permit issued by the inspections and code enforcement department. The right to construct, alter or extend any flea market shall expire 180 days after the issuance of a permit.
(b) Certificate of occupancy. It shall be unlawful and prohibited to use or permit the use of any flea market land, building or structure for which a building permit is required, and to use or permit to be used any flea market building or structure hereafter altered, extended, erected, repaired, or moved until the building inspector shall have issued a certificate of occupancy stating that the provisions of these regulations have been complied with.
(c) Occupational tax certificate. The flea market management must be issued an occupational tax certificate by the city for the operation of an indoor or outdoor flea market plus a $300.00 regulatory fee. This occupational tax certificate/license shall be a license of privilege that may be revoked by the city manager or city commission.
(1) All food service vendors shall be required to purchase an occupational tax certificate.
(2) Any vendors that may be regulated and/or governed by a state of federal regulation, must first obtain an occupational tax certificate from the city, prior to engaging in sales or services, licensed for business specifically at the flea market location by the city;
(3) A city occupational tax certificate, certificate of occupancy, required state license, or federal license or valid certificate of registration shall be continuously displayed in a conspicuous location on the front of each flea market booth.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
620:
(a) Flea market location. No flea market structure or facility shall be located within 300 feet of any residential zoning district boundary.
(b) Zoning district requirements. Flea markets shall comply with all zoning ordinance area, height, setback, lot coverage, and signage requirements of the zoning district within which the market is located. If the standards of the zoning ordinance conflict with standards of this article, the more restrictive shall apply.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
621:
(a) Condition of site not to create hazard, etc. The condition of soil, groundwater level, drainage and topography shall not create hazards to the property or the health or safety of the occupants. The site shall not be exposed to objectionable smoke, noise, odors, or other adverse influences.
(b) Soil and ground cover. Exposed ground surfaces in all parts of every flea market shall be paved, or covered with stone screenings, or other solid material, or protected with a vegetative growth that is capable of preventing soil erosion and of eliminating objectionable dust and/or mud.
(c) Site drainage requirements. The ground surface in all parts of every flea market shall be graded and equipped to drain all surface water in a safe, efficient manner in order to eliminate water pockets, low areas or bogs.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 03272023, adopted March 27, 2023, set out provisions intended for use as § 10-275. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 10-276 at the discretion of the editor.
622:
(a) All flea market structures shall be located at least 25 feet from any public street right-of-way or highway right-of-way, and at least 25 feet from the property boundary lines.
(b) All flea markets shall be provided with screening of a well-maintained opaque fence separating the market and adjacent zoning and uses, except along public road frontage used for primary access to the flea market. Said screening shall be a minimum of six feet in height.
(c) Flea market sites shall be screened from view along street right-of-way frontage used for primary access to the flea market.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 03272023, adopted March 27, 2023, set out provisions intended for use as § 10-276. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 10-277 at the discretion of the editor.
623:
(a) Streets and roads. All flea markets shall be provided with safe and convenient vehicular access from abutting public streets, or roads, or highways. Access shall not be permitted from residential streets. Access to flea markets shall be designed to minimize congestion and hazards at the entrance or exit and allow free movement of traffic on adjacent streets. The entrance road connecting the market with a public street or road shall comply with the requirements of section 6.02a.(7) of the city zoning ordinance.
(b) Walks. All pedestrian access to every flea market shall be paved, and shall be of adequate width for the intended use. Sudden changes in alignment and gradient shall be avoided.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 03272023, adopted March 27, 2023, set out provisions intended for use as § 10-277. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 10-278 at the discretion of the editor.
624:
(a) Quantity. Off-street parking areas shall be provided in all flea markets. Such areas shall be furnished at the rate of 5.5 spaces per 1,000 square feet of gross sales area.
(b) Area required. The area required for a parking space for one vehicle shall consist of 300 square feet of lot area, including the parking stall and access aisle.
(c) Space dimensions. A parking space, exclusive of the area required for access to the space, shall be of an area not less than nine feet wide by 20 feet long for each motor vehicle, such space being fully accessible for the storage or parking of permitted vehicles.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 03272023, adopted March 27, 2023, set out provisions intended for use as § 10-278. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 10-279 at the discretion of the editor.
625:
(a) Structural requirements. All structures, to include booths, shall comply with the city building code.
(b) Booths. Flea market booths shall be of a standard design approved by the building inspection department, and shall be provided to all vendors by the flea market management.
(c) Stands. The flea market stand shall be constructed of materials that will provide an adequate foundation for the placement of flea market booths, thereby securing the superstructure against uplift, sliding, rotation and overturning. The flea market stands shall not heave, shift or settle unevenly under the weight of the flea market booth due to inadequate drainage, vibration, or other forces acting on the superstructure.
(d) Identification. Each booth shall be numbered. Each number shall be easily identified from the nearest street, driveway, or walkway.
(e) Signs. Flea market signs are subject to the provisions of the zoning district within which the flea market is located, and subject to the requirements in section 111-366, article X, signs.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 03272023, adopted March 27, 2023, set out provisions intended for use as § 10-279. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 10-280 at the discretion of the editor.
626:
(a) Water supply. An accessible, adequate, safe and potable supply of water shall be provided in each flea market. Where a public supply of water of satisfactory quantity, quality and pressure is available, connection shall be made thereto and its supply used exclusively. When a satisfactory public water supply is not available, a private water supply system may be developed and used as approved by the state department of public health and the state department of natural resources in accordance with rules and regulations for water supply quality control and other applicable rules and regulations. The water supply system of the flea market shall be constructed and connected in accordance with the plumbing code in force in the city.
(b) Transient hookup facilities. Transient water, sewer and electrical hookup facilities shall be provided for weekend (Friday through Sunday only) overnight campers, motor homes, travel trailers and recreational vehicles (including self-contained), not to exceed 72 hours in any one week. All vehicle hookups shall comply with the requirements of the plumbing code in force in the city. The number of such vehicles on site overnight shall not exceed the number of operating overnight hookups provided. At no time shall any overnight camper, motor home, travel trailer, or recreational vehicle utilize any electrical, sewer, or water connection provided for a flea market booth.
(c) Restrooms and sewage disposal. There shall be a minimum of one permanent central restroom facility located on the premises. Within that central restroom there shall be separate facilities for men and women. Restroom shall be located within 300 feet of travel distance.
(1) Hot and cold water shall be furnished to every lavatory and sink; cold water shall be furnished to every water closet and urinal.
(2) Liquid soap, contained in dispensing units, paper towels, and toilet paper shall be provided in every restroom.
(3) Restrooms shall contain at least the minimum of fixtures required by the plumbing code in force in the city.
(4) All flea markets shall be connected to the city water and sewer system in accordance with section 38-64 and section 38-192.
(d) Electrical distribution system. Every flea market shall contain electrical wiring systems for each flea market stand requiring electricity. Electrical distribution systems shall be installed and maintained in accordance with applicable electric codes of the city.
(e) Fire hydrants. Fire hydrants shall be installed as required by Douglas Fire Department and in City Code chapter 18 in article II.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 03272023, adopted March 27, 2023, set out provisions intended for use as § 10-280. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 10-281 at the discretion of the editor.
629:
The flea market site shall not be exposed to objectionable smoke, noise, odors or other adverse influences.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
630:
Flea markets shall be subject to all fire prevention ordinances of the city.
(1) Litter. Flea markets shall be kept free of litter, rubbish and other flammable materials.
(2) Fire extinguishers. Portable fire extinguishers of a type approved by the fire prevention bureau shall be kept in service buildings and at all other locations designated by the fire prevention bureau, and shall be maintained in good operating condition.
(3) Cooking.
a. Fires shall be made only in stoves, incinerators and other equipment intended for cooking.
b. Cooking shelters, barbecue pits, fireplaces, grills, and woodburning stoves shall be so located, constructed, maintained, and used as to avoid fire hazards and smoke nuisance, both on the property on which used, and on neighboring property.
c. No fuel shall be used, and no material burned which emits dense smoke or objectionable odors.
d. No refuse shall be burned on the premises of the flea markets at any time.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
631:
(a) All vendors intending to engage in the sale of prepared food items at the flea market shall first obtain a permit from the county health department for the flea market location before applying for an occupational tax certificate.
(b) All vendors intending to engage in retail food sales operations at the flea market location shall first obtain a license from the county health department and/or state department of agriculture. All retail food sales licenses shall be continuously displayed in a conspicuous location on the front of the booth where said activity has been licensed to occur.
(c) All food shall meet health department regulations.
(d) Any vendor requiring a food service permit or retail food sales license shall at all times conspicuously display said permit on the front of the vending booth where said activity has been licensed to occur at all times.
(e) All food vendors m must pay an occupational tax certificate fee from the city.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
632:
The storage, collection, and disposal of refuse in the flea market shall be conducted so as to create no health hazards, rodent harborage, insect breeding areas, accidents, fire hazards, or air pollution. No building permit shall be issued until the solid waste director approves the proposed plans for the storage and collection of solid waste.
(1) Refuse storage. All refuse shall be stored in fly-tight, watertight, rodentproof containers provided by the flea market management. Such containers shall be provided in sufficient numbers and capacity to properly store all refuse. The containers may be placed at the curbside for collection only on days of the scheduled collection. At other times, containers shall be located in a protected manner and restricted from general view.
(2) Refuse collection stands. Where refuse collection stands are provided for common or joint use, such stands shall be located not more than 100 feet from a using flea market stand, and shall be so designed as to: prevent containers from being tipped; minimize spillage and container deterioration; and facilitate cleaning around them. Refuse collection containers shall be located throughout the flea market for the convenient use of patrons.
(3) Bulk waste containers. Where bulk waste containers of at least three cubic yards are utilized, a suitable concrete pad shall be provided for parking the container. Such pads shall be supplied with a drain connected to sewage disposal facilities, and available water connections convenient for washing the container.
(4) Refuse collection. All refuse shall be collected at least weekly; up to six times per week if the amount of refuse generated requires more frequent pickup. Where suitable collection service is not available from municipal or private agencies, the flea market management shall provide this service. All refuse shall be collected and transported in covered vehicles or covered containers to the disposal site designated by the city.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
633:
Grounds, buildings, and structures shall be maintained free of insect and rodent harborage and infestation. Extermination methods and other measures to control insects and rodents shall conform with the requirements of the county health department.
(1) Debris. Flea markets shall be maintained free of accumulations of debris which may provide rodent harborage or breeding places for flies, mosquitoes, and other pests.
(2) Storage areas. Storage areas shall be so maintained as to prevent rodent harborage; lumber, pipe and other building materials shall be stored at least one foot above the ground.
(3) Structural gaps. Where the potential for insect and rodent infestation exists, all exterior openings, in or beneath any structure, shall be appropriately screened with wire mesh or other suitable materials.
(4) Weeds. The growth of brush, weeds, and grass shall be controlled so as to prevent the harborage of ticks, chiggers, and other noxious insects. Flea markets shall be so maintained as to prevent the growth of ragweed, poison ivy, poison oak, poison sumac and other noxious weeds considered detrimental to health. Open areas shall be maintained free of heavy undergrowth.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
634:
Natural gas, liquefied petroleum, fuel oil, and any other fuel supply or fuel storage piping systems shall be installed and maintained in accordance with applicable fuel gas codes, and gas codes in force in the city.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
635:
The sale of animals is prohibited in any flea market, including, but not limited to reptiles, birds, felines, and canines.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
636:
The person to whom a license for flea market operation is issued (the flea market manager) shall operate a flea market in compliance with all applicable laws and ordinances, and shall provide adequate supervision to maintain the park, landscaping, fences, and its facilities and equipment in good repair, and in a clean and sanitary condition. The flea market management shall be available to any city department, official, or agency during all hours of flea market operation, for the purpose of enforcing compliance with the requirements of this article.
(1) The flea market management shall notify market tenants of all applicable provisions of this article, and inform them of their duties and responsibilities under this article and the regulations issued hereunder.
(2) The flea market management shall supervise the placement of each flea market booth on its stand which includes securing its stability and installing all utility connections.
(3) The flea market management shall immediately notify the county health department of any suspected communicable or contagious disease within the flea market.
(4) The flea market management shall notify the inspections and code enforcement department of any overnight campers, motor homes, travel trailers, and recreational vehicles remaining on the flea market site in violation of subsection 16-194(b).
(5) The flea market management shall not rent, lease, nor otherwise provide space to any vendor not in possession of a city occupational tax certificate, unless a certificate of registration has been issued, and daily retail sales fee has been collected in accordance with subsection 16-167(c). All such registration receipts and sales fees shall be delivered to the license inspector at the end of every business week.
(6) The flea market management shall not allow any vendor to sell foodstuffs unless that vendor displays a valid retail food sales license, and/or a food service permit, as required in section 16-214.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
639:
Department means the city marshal or his/her designee.
Farmers market means an operation at a designated location used primarily for the distribution and sale directly to consumers of food products by farmers or other food producers of agricultural products. A farmers' market for the purposes of section 16-135 does not include a "flea market" or a retail grocery store.
Sampling shall mean a food product promotion where only a bite-sized portion of food is offered free of charge to demonstrate its characteristics and shall not consist of a whole meal, an individual portion, or a whole sandwich.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
640:
(a) General provisions.
(1) No person shall operate a farmers market without a valid occupational tax certificate. A copy shall be conspicuously posted at the site of the farmers market.
(2) Farmers markets shall be located only on appropriately zoned property. The owner or operator of the farmers market shall obtain written permission from the property owner stating that the market has permission to vend food on the property. The letter containing written permission letter shall be submitted to the director along with the occupational tax certificate.
(3) Conveniently located, commercial, fixed-plumbed toilet facilities shall be available for market vendors and patrons. A notarized letter from the business owner granting the market vendors access to toilet facilities during all hours of the farmers market operation shall be submitted with the occupational tax certificate application. A copy of the letter shall be made available to the director upon request. All toilets shall conform to the city code and shall have tight fitting, self-closing solid doors. Toilet rooms and fixtures shall be clean and in good repair. Toilet paper shall be available and easily accessible at all times. Toilets accessible to women shall have a trash receptacle that is covered with a lid.
(4) A handwash lavatory with hot and cold water under pressure and tempered through a mixing valve shall be provided in or immediately adjacent to the toilet room. A soap dispenser and disposable paper towels shall be available at all times. All wastewater shall be captured and disposed of in an approved sewage disposal system.
(5) The permit holder shall ensure that all trash, refuse and garbage is removed from the site at the end of each day or that trash, refuse and garbage is placed in appropriate containers for later disposal. The premises occupied by the farmers market shall be kept clean and free of accumulated trash, refuse or garbage during and after the hours of operation. All trash, refuse and garbage that remains at the market site shall be sealed in plastic bags and discarded in waste containers. Sufficient durable, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable, leak proof, rodent and insect proof refuse and garbage containers shall be available on site.
(6) It shall be unlawful for any farmers market manager or agent to allow food vendors or mobile food vendors to engage in food preparation or sales without the food vendor or mobile food vendor obtaining an occupational tax certificate and meeting all state and local requirements, other than that involved in sampling.
(b) Sale and distribution of produce or food at farmers markets.
(1) Produce and food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly represented to the consumer.
(2) Produce and food sold at a farmers market must comply with applicable state and federal laws.
(3) Packaged food sold or distributed at farmers markets shall be labeled in accordance with the requirements of applicable state and federal laws.
(4) Food displays shall be confined to tables or to the bed of a vehicle. Food must be at least six inches above the ground.
(5) Fresh produce shall not be cut or sliced.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
641:
Any person, firm, corporation, or entity commits an offense if that person violates any provision of this section, or fails to perform an act required by this section shall be punished in accordance to section 1-11.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
643:
The purpose of the pop-up market/installation special event permit is to allow retail entrepreneurs, cultural events providers and restaurateurs to operate temporarily in the city. These provisions apply exclusively to town center, gateway, general commercial, neighborhood commercial, parks, schools, and churches. Pop-up activities will enable organizers to establish a short-term retail, cultural or culinary installation within specific guidelines based on the nature of the operation.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
644:
As used in this chapter, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:
Pop-up market/installation means an establishment that operates on a temporary basis in a specific location, building or portion thereof, for the sale of merchandise, provision of services to the public, display or cultural exhibitions, or to achieve a particular goal.
Pop-up retail user means any merchant who occupies or leases for 14 days or less a for retail space for the sale of merchandise or provision of services.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
645:
Temporary indoor corporate, retail or cultural installations held within the City of Douglas, leased for 14 days or less must receive approval for a temporary business use in the form of a pop-up special event permit. This approval will be given for a maximum of 14 days:
(1) Zoning, building and licensing approval from the City of Douglas. No changes of use will be permitted (e.g., vacant retail shall remain retail/mercantile; restaurant use will be permitted only for locations already in use as a restaurant, etc.). Additionally, no construction or alteration to the space may occur without triggering a building permit requirement and its associated plans review.
(2) A fire inspection report may be required.
(3) Written permission of the land owner.
(4) State license, if applicable.
(5) The applicant shall pay an application fee of $100.00 occupational tax plus a $200.00 regulatory fee filed.
(6) Food vendors must comply with a state laws and regulations, and local ordinances;
a. Adhere local health department rules and regulations; and
b. Obtain the approval of any applicable public agency including but not limited to: City of Douglas and the Coffee County Health Department.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
646:
A person commits an offense if that person violates any provision of this section, or fails to perform an act required by this section shall be punished in accordance to section 1-11.
(Ord. No. 03272023, 3-27-2023)
649:
The purpose of this article is to support and regulate small-scale food entrepreneurs operating from residential/home kitchens, referred to as cottage food operators, in accordance with the Georgia Cottage Food Program and the rules of the Georgia Department of Agriculture. The City of Douglas seeks to promote economic development in rural areas while ensuring public health and safety.
(Ord. No. 05122025(2), § 1, 5-12-2025)
650:
For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply:
Cottage food license means a permit issued by the Georgia Department of Agriculture under its cottage food program.
Cottage food operation means a person who produces non-potentially hazardous food items in a home kitchen for direct sale to consumers, in compliance with the Georgia Department of Agriculture cottage food license.
Direct sale means sale directly to the end consumer including at farmers markets, roadside stands, events, or via online platforms with local delivery or pickup.
Non-potentially hazardous food means foods that do not require time/temperature control for safety, as listed by the Georgia Department of Agriculture.
Operator means the person responsible for the cottage food production who resides in the home where the food is produced.
Residential/home kitchen means a residential kitchen located in a private primary residence.
(Ord. No. 05122025(2), § 2, 5-12-2025)
651:
(a) All cottage food operators must obtain a valid cottage food license from the Georgia Department of Agriculture prior to beginning food production.
(b) Operators must obtain an annual occupational tax certificate (business license) with the City of Douglas Community Development Department, providing:
(1) A copy of their state-issued cottage food license;
(2) Proof of residency;
(3) A signed statement agreeing to comply with all applicable regulations.
(c) Operators must notify the city of any change in ownership, location, or business cessation within 30 days.
(d) Operators shall comply with all applicable health, labeling, packaging, and operational standards set by the Georgia Department of Agriculture.
(e) No cottage food operation shall prepare or sell potentially hazardous food items, as defined by the Georgia Department of Agriculture.
(Ord. No. 05122025(2), § 3, 5-12-2025)
652:
(a) Food production must take place only within the operator's primary residence.
(b) No commercial-grade equipment shall be installed unless approved by local code enforcement.
(c) Direct sales to the public are permitted, including at farmers markets, roadside stands, and online with in-person delivery.
(d) No food may be shipped across state lines unless otherwise authorized by law.
(e) All packaging must clearly label:
(1) The name and address of the operator;
(2) A list of ingredients;
(3) A statement: "This product is homemade and not subject to state food safety inspection."
(f) Operators must follow safe food handling practices, as outlined in the Georgia Department of Agriculture guidelines.
(Ord. No. 05122025(2), § 4, 5-12-2025)
653:
Cottage food operations shall be permitted in all residential zoning districts within the City of Douglas, provided they:
(1) Operate only within the primary residence of the operator.
(2) Do not employ individuals outside of immediate household members.
(3) Do not generate significant traffic, noise, or disruption inconsistent with residential use.
(Ord. No. 05122025(2), § 5, 5-12-2025)
654:
The City of Douglas reserves the right to coordinate with the Georgia Department of Agriculture for periodic inspections or investigations in response to complaints or suspected violations.
(Ord. No. 05122025(2), § 6, 5-12-2025)
656:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Criminal trespass and damage to property, O.C.G.A. § 16-7-20 et seq.
660:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Bronze marker means a memorial bronze or other cast metal projecting above ground level no more than one-half inch.
City cemetery means that tract of land located within the city currently utilized for the burial of the dead and designated as the city municipal cemetery.
Columbarium means a mini mausoleum with niches designed to hold cremains.
Corner marker means a marker buried flush with the ground at the inside corners of plots or lots, the maximum dimension of which is six inches by six inches.
Cremains means the ashes of a cremated human body.
Cremation means the reduction of the body of a deceased human to its essential elements by incineration.
Funeral home means an establishment in which the dead are prepared for burial or cremation and in which wakes and funerals may be held.
Ground cover means the number, in inches, of soil material to be deposited over the burial vault and/or casket at ground level.
Lot means that tract of land capable of accommodating the burial of two individual outer burial containers.
Maintenance fee means that fee charged the owners of cemetery plots, lots or mausoleums for maintenance and upkeep of such plots, lots or mausoleums throughout the year.
Mausoleum means an aboveground structure erected for the purpose of the interment of deceased bodies.
Monument means a memorial structure consisting of granite, stone, marble or other designated manmade material marking the plot or lot in which a burial has or will take place.
Notification of burial means that notice requested to be given the city representative by the mortician or other responsible party of date and time of burial.
Outer burial containers means any concrete or steel container designed for the placement in the grave around the casket, including, but not limited to, such containers commonly known as burial vaults, grave boxes and grave liners.
Permanent marker means a marker made of a permanent material such as concrete, marble, masonry, iron, steel, or metal and identifying the name of the individual with date buried and the name of the funeral home carved, etched, sandblasted or stamped into the marker.
Permit means that document allowing burial in the city's cemetery. The permit shall be obtained prior to burial from a designated city department.
Plantings means any growth of herbaceous, annual and perennial flowers permitted to be planted on a plot or lot within the cemetery as designated by the city's representatives.
Plot means that tract of land located within the cemetery containing one or more cemetery lots.
Section means that area of the cemetery containing a number of plots and/or lots.
(Code 1978, § 8-22; Code 1993, pt. II, § 26-1; Ord. No. 05122003.01, 5-12-2003)
661:
It is hereby the intent of the mayor and board of commissioners, in order to promote the orderly development and maintenance of the municipal cemetery of the city, that the following rules, regulations and requirements shall be adopted and shall govern all interments within the cemetery.
(Code 1978, § 8-21; Code 1993, pt. II, § 26-2)
662:
(a) A legal description containing the location, dimensions, courses, distances, metes, bounds and deed references for the city cemetery shall be as shown on a map or plat retained permanently in the official map area at the city hall to be designated as the "Official Description and Plat of the City of Douglas Cemetery."
(b) Such land is hereby dedicated to cemetery use, and it shall be used for cemetery purposes only.
(c) There shall be placed on such cemetery property only graves with bronze grave markers, and such bronze grave markers shall not project or protrude above ground level.
(d) The city manager is hereby authorized and directed to do any and all acts and things necessary to manage and control the use of the above-described land for the purposes herein stated.
(Code 1978, § 8-1; Code 1993, pt. II, § 26-3)
663:
(a) Purchase of lot. Any person desiring to purchase a plot or lot within the city cemetery may do so by depositing with the city the full cost of the plot or lot selected. At the time of purchase, the purchaser shall be issued a receipt upon which is noted the plot and/or lot number, as well as the cemetery section designation, the purchase price and name and address of purchaser and any other necessary information required by the city.
(b) Purchase price. The purchase price of any lot within the city's cemetery shall be as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges. The purchaser shall waive any or all air rights over the lot purchased.
(c) Lot size. All lots sold within the city's cemetery shall measure a minimum of ten feet by ten feet.
(d) Plot size. A plot shall consist of any number of lots having a common boundary line on at least one side or end.
(Code 1978, § 8-23; Code 1993, pt. II, § 26-4)
664:
(a) Permit required. There shall be required by any party responsible for opening any grave site located on any lot within the cemetery a permit issued by a representative of the city. The permit shall be obtained a minimum of 24 hours in advance of the site opening. The notice may be waived by the city in extenuating circumstances.
(b) Permit fee. The fee charged by the city for the issuance of a permit to open a grave site shall be as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges. (c) City responsibility. (a) Dimensions. All grave sites shall have an opening sufficient in size to accommodate the casket and outer burial container.
(b) Ground cover. All graves shall be dug to a depth sufficient to allow a minimum ground cover of 18 inches.
(c) Material disposal. All excess soil removed from a grave site shall be deposited at a site designated by the city representative.
(d) Soil removal methods. In no event shall the removal of excess material result in the damage to surrounding plots and/or lots, cause ruts to develop, cause damage to surrounding trees, shrubbery, flowers, monuments, etc. In the event of such damage, the person responsible shall pay to the city its cost of repair of such damage.
(e) Soil compaction. All grave sites opened shall have the soil returned to the site fully compacted to prevent the settling of such soil after completion of the burial. The costs of any settling at the grave site that takes place within one year of the burial which requires city personnel to correct shall be charged to the party responsible for the original grave site opening.
(f) Outer burial container required. For all burials in the city cemetery, the city will require, in addition to a casket, an outer burial container approved by city officials that is made of such material and of such thickness as to render the grave site impervious to eventual cave-ins (materials such as concrete, 1½ inches thick, coated metals of 12 gauge or thicker, or manmade materials impervious to decay). Wooden boxes do not comply with this requirement.
(g) Temporary marker. The funeral home shall at the time of burial affix to the ground, displayed in a position as to be read, a temporary marker identifying the name of the individual, the date buried, and the funeral home's name carved, etched, sandblasted or stamped into the marker. The marker must be temporary affixed in such a way that the marker would not hinder maintenance of the plot.
(Code 1978, § 8-25; Code 1993, pt. II, § 26-6; Ord. No. 05122003.01, 5-12-2003)
